seoTitle: How to Charge a Card on Stripe & Request Payment
metaDescription: See three ways to collect credit card payments on Stripe: manual dashboard charges, payment links, and invoices, plus how card processing fees work.
intro: There's more than one way to get paid on Stripe, and picking the right method depends on how your business operates. This guide covers manually charging a card from the dashboard, generating a one-time payment link, and requesting payment through an invoice, along with a look at how fees apply when charging customers.

steps.heading: Review the methods to charge cards on Stripe
steps.body: Before diving in, it helps to know your three main options: a manual dashboard charge, a payment link, and an invoice — each suits a different situation.

steps.heading: Manually charge a card via the dashboard
steps.body: For a quick, one-off charge, you can enter a customer's card details directly in the Stripe dashboard and process the payment immediately.

steps.heading: Create a payment link
steps.body: For repeatable or shareable payment requests, generate a payment link customers can use to pay without you handling their card details directly.

steps.heading: Use invoices to request payment
steps.body: For service-based or recurring work, send an invoice through Stripe so the customer can review the charge and pay on their own time.

faq.question: What's the easiest way to charge a customer once on Stripe?
faq.answer: A manual dashboard charge or a one-time payment link are the quickest options for a single, non-recurring payment.

faq.question: Do fees change depending on how I charge the card?
faq.answer: Processing fees generally apply to card transactions regardless of the method, though international cards can carry different rates.

faq.question: Can I request payment without exposing my customer's card details to me?
faq.answer: Yes, payment links and invoices let customers enter their own card details securely without you handling that information directly.

faq.question: Is this method suitable for freelancers as well as stores?
faq.answer: Yes, the guide covers approaches that work whether you're running an online store, a service business, or freelancing.
